abstract: Can independent randomizations of integer-line constraints supply dense configurations that survive partial restoration of the true geometry? We study a cap-preserving product-label model: each primitive nonaxis direction receives independent row and column permutations, while actual row and column caps remain two. For $m=\lfloor cn\rfloor$ and $A=3/\pi^2$, its expected solution count satisfies $\log\mathbb E Z=(c-Ac^3)n\log n+O_c(n)$. Above $c_* =\pi/\sqrt3$, existence is exponentially unlikely on the $n\log n$ scale. Below $c_*$, exponentially many solutions occur with probability at least $e^{-O_c(n)}$, including densities above $1.8$. The proof combines geometric forcing of canonical permutation events, finite-direction entropy, and an orbit second moment. Common supports survive bounded whole-direction restoration and bounded entry fixing in every direction, including intermediate swaps. For a fixed fraction $\rho$ of empty marked source labels, a clean-path forcing argument gives the sharp annealed coefficient $c-A(1-\rho)^{-6}c^3$ and an $e^{-O(n)}$ abundance bound below $c_*(1-\rho)^3$. A separate affine-conic seed argument restores a sufficiently small positive fraction of occupied points in every direction while retaining density above $1.8$, with an explicit probability form $\exp(-O_c(\rho)n\log n-O_{c,\rho}(n))$. Both macroscopic results tolerate every deletion order within a prescribed marked set. A turnover bound explains why many starting solutions require macroscopic point replacement to reach dense physical endpoints. Exact finite controls check the proof interfaces. The results do not establish typical subcritical feasibility, an efficient sampler, full restoration, or an unbounded true-grid construction.

change_summary: Strengthens empty-strip Theorem6 to sharp annealed entropy and an exp(-Cn) subcritical abundance bound via logarithmic path truncation, clean-event mass control and a uniform forcing estimate. Adds Theorem7 for a positive fraction of occupied marked labels using an affine-conic seed, complete resource inventories, a uniform scalar mass functional and short-direction entropy. Adds five exact interface controls. Clarifies the uniform capped law and cites and distinguishes papers6v5,7v1,14v1 as requested by the v1 reviewer. No physical-grid construction is claimed.

coauthors.contribution: Independent proof audits; finite-direction entropy and orbit assembly; whole-direction restoration; macroscopic cycle-path lower bound; occupied-label affine-conic seed theorem, explicit resource and mass analysis, and exact controls; turnover corollary.

title: Annealed entropy and coupled restoration in a cap-preserving randomized line model
